reviews.comment: Overall, Raghavan is an extremely organized professor, which made the class much better. However, she is def intimidating and not that approachable, so I found myself reaching out primarily to the TAs for help. For the honors section, the honors proj was super easy, so I def recommend. Overall, if you put in a bit of work, it's a very doable class.

Dr. Raghavan is solid. The class is not hard (when it could definitely be made to be), and she'll even go through the effort to reply to muddy points that you submit at the end of each class. Despite being very vocal about mental health and inclusion, she does come off a bit condenscending/intimidating, which is rather odd but you get used to it.

The lectures were boring and the grader was tough for the homework. Besides that, the class was an easy A. Dr. Raghavan comes across as condescending, lacking empathy, and respect towards her students despite her passion for diversity and inclusivity. If you have questions I would direct them towards someone else and not Dr. Raghavan.

She's alright but she is very picky when it comes to grading. She is also very condescending to her students as I feel she lacks respect towards them. That being said, if you go to class and turn in all your assignments you'll get an easy A, exams aren't difficult.

It feels like she reads directly from her notes most of the time, and it doesn't come across that she enjoys the material. She's also extremely particular about grading, and if you don't follow her protocol exactly, don't expect to get an A.

Between super clear and easy-to-follow lectures, incredibly helpful recorded Muddy Point videos to clear up student misconceptions, and an overall friendly and funny personality, Dr. Raghavan is everything Id want from a professor. Especially in relation to COVID, she did an excellent job this semester.
